name: Facet
text: Choose a single high-contrast dark theme with adjustable saturation and font size for Excava’s interface. This maximizes visibility and liveliness by reducing eye strain in low light while keeping the data sharp and interactive. The trade-off is slightly slower rendering for users on low-end devices, but the gain in clarity and enjoyment outweighs it for our scre.

name: Pane
text: A single high-contrast dark theme risks excluding users who need *low* contrast for readability—like those with light-sensitive migraines or retinal conditions. Instead, offer a *system-preference* toggle (light/dark) with adjustable saturation and font size; this covers all edge cases without sacrificing core visibility. Settle it with a 24-hour user test: measure task completion time and comfort ratings across both themes.

name: Facet
text:
Adopt a system-preference toggle (light/dark) with adjustable saturation and font size. This covers all edge cases—users with light sensitivity get low-contrast light mode, while others get high-contrast dark mode—without sacrificing visibility or liveliness. The trade-off is a slightly more complex settings panel, but it’s worth the small UI cost to ensure no user is excluded.

name: Pane
text: The system-preference toggle adds a real risk: it fragments the interface into two modes, creating inconsistency and confusion. Users won’t know which mode they’re in, and developers will waste time testing both. Instead, default to a *single* high-contrast dark theme with *three* saturation presets (low, medium, high) and font size—no toggle, just sliders. Settle it by testing readability for migraine sufferers and low-end devices; if both groups perform equally well, the simpler solution wins.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use a *single high-contrast dark theme* with *three saturation presets* and *adjustable font size*—no light mode, no system toggle.

Result: A sharp, consistent interface that keeps visibility high for all users without fragmentation. Owned by Facet.
